title: The Kitchen of Rosewater Lane
premise: Quentin Eriksen, a ghostwriter hiding from the scandal that ended his legal career, has spent three years ghosting a rival's memoirs while exchanging anonymous letters with a stranger who once wrote to a prison address by mistake. When the letter-writer, Marisol Vance, moves next door and recognizes his voice, she also becomes the only witness to the corruption his rival is laundering through the memoir — and the only person who can prove Quentin was framed a decade ago. As Quentin must choose between the safe smallness of his rebuilt life and the justice Marisol insists is owed, she is drawn into danger when the rival realizes what she knows. The story ends with Quentin testifying outside the protection of any deal, Marisol staying past the last train to stand with him, and the two building a fragile, honest life on Rosewater Lane.
about_author: Oscar Dunmore is the pen name of a former court reporter who spent twelve years transcribing other people's confessions before turning them into fiction. He lives above a bakery, writes at night, and insists every love story is really a story about testimony.

chapters.title: The Last Train Schedule
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. He finishes a chapter of his rival Aldous Wren's memoir, then walks the platform to watch the last train leave — his nightly ritual of safety. A letter arrives with a new postmark: Rosewater Lane. Emotional beat: the ache of a life built entirely out of exits.

chapters.title: Moving Vans and Mistaken Addresses
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. She moves into the house next door, carrying a shoebox of a decade of unsent letters. She hears Quentin's voice through the hedge and freezes — it matches the letters. Emotional beat: recognition and the terror of being known.

chapters.title: The Hedge Between Us
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. He realizes the new neighbor is his letter-writer and pretends not to know. They share tomatoes over the fence, both performing casualness. Emotional beat: intimacy disguised as small talk, and guilt over the deception.

chapters.title: What the Memoir Leaves Out
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Hired to fact-check Wren's memoir, she finds a gap where a whistleblower — Quentin — should be. She cross-references the letters. Emotional beat: the cold thrill of connecting evidence to the man next door.

chapters.title: Three Years of Small Steps
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV, flashback woven in. The disbarment, the frame job, the prison letter that started everything — a stranger who wrote to the wrong address and kept writing. Emotional beat: how safety became its own kind of sentence.

chapters.title: You Write Like Someone Confessing
chapters.summary: Marisol confronts Quentin gently over coffee, quoting his letters back to him. He denies nothing and everything. Emotional beat: the vertigo of being seen without armor.

chapters.title: Wren's Version of Events
chapters.summary: Wren's POV (single chapter). Charming, wounded, ruthless, he reviews the manuscript and senses a loose thread named Marisol Vance. Emotional beat: corruption wearing the face of grievance.

chapters.title: The Shoebox on the Kitchen Table
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. She lays ten years of letters across Quentin's kitchen table and asks why he never wrote back under his own name. Emotional beat: grief for the years fear cost them both.

chapters.title: A Witness With a Lease
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. He begs Marisol to drop the fact-checking; she refuses, arguing justice doesn't wait for people to feel ready. Their first real fight. Emotional beat: love arriving as friction, not comfort.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. He offers Quentin co-credit and a clean record in exchange for Marisol's silence — a bribe shaped like a gift. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: Rosewater Lane at Night
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. A break-in; her shoebox is searched, nothing taken but a single letter. Quentin finds her shaking on his porch. Emotional beat: fear making the choice for them — or so they think.

chapters.title: What Was Taken
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The stolen letter is the one proving Wren knew about the falsified evidence. Quentin realizes Wren isn't cleaning up the memoir; he's erasing Quentin's exoneration. Emotional beat: safety officially dead.

chapters.title: The Archivist
chapters.summary: Both POVs alternating. They seek an old prison librarian who kept copies of inmate correspondence — justice through unofficial channels. Emotional beat: hope found in the margins of institutions.

chapters.title: Copies and Consequences
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The librarian confirms duplicates exist but warns Wren has friends in the bar association. Marisol's job offer is quietly revoked. Emotional beat: the price of witnessing made concrete.

chapters.title: Quentin's Confession, Draft One
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. He ghostwrites his own testimony at the kitchen table, Marisol editing — the ghostwriter finally signing his own work. Emotional beat: reclaiming authorship of his life.

chapters.title: The Last Train Leaves Without Them
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Wren's people escalate; the pair must relocate the duplicate letters before dawn. Marisol misses the last train deliberately and stays at Quentin's. Emotional beat: choosing to stay as an act of courage.

chapters.title: What Wren Knows
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Cornered, he decides to destroy the letters and Quentin's credibility in one move, scheduling a public memoir launch as cover. Emotional beat: power revealing its panic.

chapters.title: The Launch
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. At Wren's glittering book launch, Quentin walks in uninvited to read his own chapter aloud — the one Wren cut. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into voice.

chapters.title: Testimony Without a Deal
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Before journalists and a bar investigator, Quentin testifies with no immunity negotiated — Marisol's insistence that justice outside the law means no bargains. Emotional beat: the cost and the clean air of it.

chapters.title: Aftermath on Rosewater Lane
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Wren's empire cracks; Quentin faces an uncertain reinstatement; the letters are returned, one missing forever. Emotional beat: exhaustion, tenderness, the strangeness of safety that isn't small.

chapters.title: The Letter He Writes Himself
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. He writes Marisol a letter under his own name and slips it under her door — the first honest correspondence between them. Emotional beat: love as signature, not anonymity.

chapters.title: Staying Past the Last Train
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV, closing. She never checks the schedule again. On the porch, over tomatoes, they plan a small, unguarded life. Final beat: belonging chosen daily, not escaped into.
